title: Source
description: A publication or supplement that content originates from.

title.description: The book's full name, as printed on it.

shelfName.description: What this book is called on the site, when that differs from its full title. The Player's Handbook is titled 'Star Wars 5e Player's Handbook' and is called 'Player's Handbook' everywhere a reader meets it.

abbreviation.description: The short form shown on a content row: PHB, SnV.

publishedAt.description: The date this edition was published.

isOfficial.description: Whether this is a licensed Star Wars product. It is not, for everything published here: Star Wars 5e is community work built on the D&D 5e SRD. Leave it off. This is not the setting that marks a book as homebrew.

isCoreRulebook.description: True for the one book that teaches the game, as opposed to the ones that extend it. The site sends a reader who arrives knowing nothing to this book, and draws its chapters as the path they are walked down. Exactly one source should set it.

blurb.description: One line a reader can use to decide whether they care about this book. Shown under its name on the sources page.

accent.description: The hue this book is drawn in wherever it is named. A closed set rather than a colour, so a book cannot be given one that fails contrast against either theme.

order.description: Where this book sits when the books are listed together. Absent means unplaced, and an unplaced book is listed after the placed ones by name.

licenseNote.description: The licensing this book is published under, in the words the licence asks for. Shown wherever the book is cited.

attribution.description: Who to credit, when that is not simply the publisher.

showOnHomePage.description: Whether this book appears on the front page shelf. The book stays browsable and searchable either way; only its place on the front page changes.

homebrew.description: Tick this for a book somebody wrote for their own table, rather than one of the Star Wars 5e books. Homebrew is kept out of the front page shelf, and everything published into it inherits the answer, so a feat in a homebrew book is homebrew without being marked one by one.
